summary: Near-real-time Sysmon-enriched SIEM export with STIX mapping and deterministic per-record pseudonymization for SOC ingest
description:
Issue summary: Customer requests a near-real-time export stream tailored for their SOC (Sentinel Financial) that includes Sysmon-style enrichment, STIX 2.1 mapping, and deterministic per-record pseudonymization so their security analysts can ingest events into their SIEM with stable identifiers across replays.

Impact: Customer cannot onboard Redwood audit stream into their managed SOC pipeline due to lack of required enrichment fields, inconsistent identifiers after redaction, and missing STIX mapping. This blocks production monitoring for 40 internal services and delays regulatory evidence handover for upcoming audit.

Requested deliverables:
- Continuous HTTPS push or mTLS webhook delivering NDJSON with one event per line, throughput ~200 eps sustained, burst to 2k eps.
- Each event populated with Sysmon-like fields (ProcessId, Image, CommandLine, ParentProcessImage, NetworkConnection fields, UserDomain, LogonId).
- STIX 2.1 JSON envelope per event or a companion mapping file that deterministically maps Redwood audit schema to STIX object types.
- Deterministic pseudonymization scheme: per-customer salt derived from HMAC(KMS-root, tenant_id) and per-entity stable pseudonyms for user, host, process across time windows. Customer requires an allowlist of raw fields (only for legal/forensics) with access controls.
- Resume tokens for guaranteed-at-least-once delivery and idempotent replay semantics.
- Delivery manifest with checkpoints and per-batch HMAC (customer requests RFC 3161-style timestamp included).

Environment / context: Production tenant for Sentinel Financial, dedicated enterprise contract. Customer uses Splunk ES and a managed SOC that prefers STIX translation at source. They have strict evidence requirements for chain-of-custody and replays for incident investigations.

Steps customer took: Enabled audit-export in Console -> Selected "webhook-typed" delivery and attempted a test delivery to their staging collector. Received events but lacked process/commandline fields and identifiers changed after redaction.

Relevant links and logs:
- Console export config: https://console.redwood.ai/tenants/sentinel/export/1432
- Sample received payload (customer provided): https://s3.amazonaws.com/sentinel-bucket/samples/redwood-missing-fields.ndjson
- Customer SOC runbook: https://sentinel.internal/docs/redwood-onboard

Desired timeline: Customer requests a working POC stream and mapping within 7 business days for security onboarding and audit evidence readiness.

investigation_notes: Checked existing export pipelines: current webhook export supports NDJSON and per-batch manifests but does not emit Sysmon-specific enrichment fields by default.
Pseudonymization currently uses non-deterministic UUIDs generated at export time; need to introduce tenant-scoped HMAC(KMS) salt to produce stable hashes for identifiers.
STIX mapping present as an internal mapping prototype but not exposed as an export option — mapping needs normalization and documentation for STIX 2.1 compliance.
Estimated runtime cost: adding HMAC per event will add CPU; at 2k eps bursts need to validate worker scaling and possible offloading to native crypto library on serving nodes.
Risk: exposing an allowlist for raw fields requires access-control gating in console and audit logs to satisfy evidence requirements.
proposed_workaround: Workaround: Provide a near-term patch that augments the webhook payload with an additional 'redwood_enrichment' object containing Sysmon-like fields derived from existing metadata where available, and attach a temporary deterministic pseudonym map generated via a per-request HMAC with a short-lived salt. This will be marked experimental and gated to sentinel tenant only.
deliverables: POC webhook endpoint that delivers STIX 2.1-compatible objects (one per event)
Deterministic pseudonymization library integrated into export path (configurable per-tenant)
Resume-token and checkpointed manifest attached to each batch with HMAC and RFC 3161 timestamp
Console toggle and access-control for raw-field allowlist
Documentation page and example Splunk ingestion recipe
resolution_notes: In progress: Engineering validated HMAC-based deterministic pseudonymization using KMS-derived tenant salt in a canary branch. Next steps: performance test at burst loads, security review for allowlist gating, and schedule a POC with Sentinal Financial on 2026-03-18. Provided customer with temporary enrichment shim and example STIX mapping JSON for testing.
